details:
Q1: #6667 is not on the default branch yet, and both plans forbid starting without it. How should this issue proceed?
Choices:
A) Hold this issue until #6667 merges into `main`, then `/reclarify` it. Nothing is built before then. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Build on the integration branch `orchestrator/project-6664` by adding an `Integration branch:` header. This goes against both plans' "dispatch after #6667 merges into the default branch" decision (Q10 A / Q27 A).
C) Treat #6667 as already merged and this checkout as stale; go ahead against `main` as it is today. **Note:** if the preflight greps still fail during planning, this choice bounces straight back to re-clarification.
Q2: The 9 gaps cover two 4-phase plans. How should the work be split?
Choices:
A) Run it as orchestrator work: use each plan's own phase order (capacity-wait phases 1–4; tiers phases 1–4), one PR per phase, with this issue kept only as the record of the gaps. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Split in two: this issue covers the capacity-wait plan (gaps 1–5, its phases in order, one PR per phase), and gaps 6–9 move to a new issue for the tiers plan.
C) Ship all 9 gaps in one PR from this issue. **Note:** this goes against the capacity-wait plan's Phase 1 rule that the off switch defaults to `false` until the resume pass exists, and it will exceed the per-issue time budget.
